newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile police arrest German colony leader Hopp.
newsitem.headline: Chile police arrest German colony leader Hopp.

text.p: Chilean police on Friday arrested one of the leaders of a mysterious German colony when he returned to the country from Argentina with four other settlers.
A radio report said police detained the man, Hartmut Hopp, on arrival at Santiago's international airport on a flight from Mendoza, Argentina.
Hours earlier, a Chilean judge issued arrest warrants against Hopp and his wife, Dorothea Witthahn, after they failed to attend a court hearing on Thursday on charges they illegally adopted a boy.
"We are sending arrest warrants against Dr. Hopp and his wife ... to the international police," said Jorge Norambuena, judge at the court in the town of Parral 200 miles (320 km) south of Santiago.

The couple flew to Mendoza accompanied by the boy, Michael, and Rebeca Schaefer, the daughter of the enclave's fugitive founder Paul Schaefer, who has been accused of sexually molesting boys at the colony, called Dignity Colony.
Norambuena issued an international arrest warrant last year against Schaefer but police have been unable to detain him despite numerous raids at the colony.

Hopp and the others left Chile the same day as two young fugitives from the colony were giving evidence to another judge, Hernan Gonzalez, who is investigating claims that Schaefer abused at least five boys at the colony's boarding school.
Tobias Muller, a 24-year old German, and Chilean Gonzalo Luna escaped from the settlement last week and have been staying at a German diplomat's house in Santiago.
Media reported that Muller and Luna told the judge that Schaefer, who has not been seen in public in recent years, is holed up in the heavily guarded enclave he founded in 1961.

A former Protestant preacher and charismatic speaker, Schaefer has been accused of assaulting boys at Dignity Colony since 1966. Media reports have said he left Germany around 1957 after charges of fondling youngsters at an orphange he founded in Bonn.
He and other leaders also face charges of illegal detention of children, obstruction of justice and tax fraud.
Defectors from the colony say residents are not allowed to read newspapers or watch television, their mail is censored, youngsters are drugged and given unusual punishments by Schaefer.
